sections.h2: Where is Trumbull, CT, and who are its neighbors?
sections.html:
Trumbull is a town in Fairfield County, part of the Greater Bridgeport Planning Region, and it borders the cities of Bridgeport and Shelton plus the towns of Stratford, Fairfield, Easton and Monroe. The 2020 census counted 36,827 residents.

The town covers 23.5 square miles, of which 23.3 is land. Elevation runs from about 40 feet above sea level at Beach Park to 615 feet at the top of Monitor Hill. That spread means a Trumbull house can be on level ground near the Pequonnock River or on a hillside lot, and the two sell differently.

Because the town sits next to Bridgeport, Fairfield and Stratford, a Trumbull address is easy to compare with homes across the line.

sections.h2: How did Trumbull become its own town?
sections.html:
Trumbull began as part of Stratford, which English colonists founded in 1639 on land the Golden Hill Paugussett people had lived on for thousands of years. Residents of the northern part petitioned in 1725 for their own village, and the colony named it Unity.

Unity merged with Long Hill, organized in 1740, to form North Stratford in 1744. The General Assembly gave full town rights in October 1797 and named the town for Jonathan Trumbull. The aviation pioneer Igor Sikorsky lived in Trumbull while he designed and flew fixed-wing aircraft and put the helicopter into mass production.

  • 1639: Stratford settled
  • 1725: northern residents petition; village named Unity
  • 1744: Unity and Long Hill form North Stratford
  • 1797: incorporated as Trumbull

The growth that matters for house values came later. The census counts 8,641 residents in 1950, 20,379 in 1960 and 31,394 in 1970. That jump in population came in the postwar decades, so a good share of the town's houses likely date from then. Check your own deed and the assessor's record for the build year.

sections.h2: Which villages and areas make up Trumbull?
sections.html:
Trumbull is a town of villages rather than one downtown, and each has its own character. The villages listed are Trumbull Center, Long Hill, Nichols, Daniels Farm and Tashua.

The Nichols Farms Historic District and the Christ Episcopal Church and Tashua Burial Ground are both on the National Register of Historic Places, so if your house is inside the Nichols Farms district, ask the town what that means for exterior changes before you plan work.

Green space is a selling point here. The town has 871.23 acres of park facilities, including Twin Brooks Park (83.2 acres), Indian Ledge Park (104.6 acres) and Robert G. Beach Memorial Park (331 acres). The 382-acre Pequonnock River Valley State Park was bought jointly by the town and the state in 1989 for $9,275,000.

The Tashua Recreation Facility covers 268 acres and includes the 18-hole Tashua Knolls golf course, built in 1976. The town library has two locations, and the Trumbull Historical Society keeps a museum on the Abraham Nichols farm site. National Little League of Trumbull won the 1989 Little League World Series championship game against a team from Kaohsiung, Taiwan.

sections.h2: What roads and trains serve Trumbull?
sections.html:
Three train stations sit near Trumbull: Bridgeport (4.6 miles), Stratford (4.9 miles) and Fairfield-Black Rock (5.7 miles), all on Metro-North's New Haven Line. Bridgeport's station also has Amtrak.

RouteWhat it does in Trumbull
Route 8Freeway through the southeast part of town toward Waterbury and Interstate 84
Route 15 (Merritt Parkway)Runs east to New Haven and west toward New York City
Route 25North to south, joins Route 8 at the Bridgeport line
Route 108Nichols Avenue and Huntington Turnpike, north from Stratford
Route 111Main Street, from Bridgeport's North End to Monroe
Route 127White Plains Road and Church Hill Road through the town center

The Greater Bridgeport Transit Authority runs bus service.

sections.h2: What schools and services does Trumbull have?
sections.html:
Trumbull Public Schools is the town's district, and it reported 6,868 students and 512 teachers for 2022 to 2023. The district includes Trumbull High School, two middle schools (Hillcrest and Madison) and six elementary schools: Booth Hill, Daniels Farm, Frenchtown, Jane Ryan, Middlebrook and Tashua.

Fire protection is split among three all-volunteer departments, the Long Hill Fire District (since 1921), the Nichols Fire District (since 1917) and the Trumbull Center Fire District (since 1925). Wikipedia says each handles its own tax structure and fundraising. If that still holds, your tax bill may include a district line, so check the current bill or ask the tax collector.

The Trumbull Police Department dates to 1941, and Trumbull EMS was founded in 1976.

Trumbull has a mix of retail and office space. Westfield Trumbull mall is on Route 111 at the Bridgeport line, and an office park north of the Merritt Parkway near the Shelton and Stratford borders has housed firms such as UnitedHealthcare.

The town's planning rules include professional office overlay zones along White Plains Road, Church Hill Road and Main Street, plus a mixed-use zone around the historic Long Hill Green. Those details come from an older Wikipedia summary, so confirm current zoning with the town if you own property along those corridors.

We did not confirm current employer counts, the grand list, the current mill rate or any local permit or blight rules from an official town page, so we have left them out.

sections.h2: What do Connecticut sellers file when a Trumbull house closes?
sections.html:
When the deed is recorded in Trumbull, the seller's side files Connecticut Form OP-236, the real estate conveyance tax return, with the town clerk. The Department of Revenue Services says the grantor, the grantor's attorney or an agent files it, and the return and any tax are due at recording.

Trumbull's code on the form is 144. Tax is due when the consideration reaches $2,000, unless an exemption applies. Participating towns accept the return through myCTREC, and others take paper copies with a check payable to the Commissioner of Revenue Services.

The state lists exemptions that can come up when a seller is in trouble, such as a deed of a principal residence in lieu of foreclosure and a transfer of a principal residence where the price cannot cover the mortgages and priority liens. One exemption covers a principal residence with a deteriorated concrete foundation caused by pyrrhotite, as determined by a professional engineer, and needs a copy of the engineer's evaluation. See the DRS page.

  • Form: OP-236, with schedules if there are more than two grantors or an estate or trust is selling
  • Trumbull town code: 144
  • Electronic option: myCTREC where the town participates

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Trumbull seller?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Trumbull skips the lender, so the offer is based on the house as it is and closing depends on title work and the date you pick. You send us the address and condition, and we respond with an offer you can accept or turn down.

It suits a seller with a house that has deferred work, an estate property, or a tenant situation. For a house a buyer needs to finance, the same flaws can slow things down at inspection or appraisal. If the house is fine and you have time, a listing with an agent may bring a different result, and we say so plainly.

faqs.a: Trumbull is in Fairfield County, Connecticut, and belongs to the Greater Bridgeport Planning Region.
The town has 23.5 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 36,827 residents.

faqs.q: Is there a train station in Trumbull?
faqs.a: The nearest Metro-North stations are Bridgeport (4.6 miles), Stratford (4.9 miles) and Fairfield-Black Rock (5.7 miles).

faqs.q: What do I file with the town clerk when I sell?
faqs.a: Connecticut Form OP-236, the conveyance tax return, is filed when the deed is recorded. Trumbull's town code is 144. Your closing attorney can compute the amount.

faqs.q: Will I need to repair my Trumbull house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash offer is based on the property in its current condition, so repairs are not a requirement to receive one.
